text:
Jason Robertson learned this month how close he came to being a Penguin. A Yahoo Sports report said the Stars nearly sent him to Pittsburgh on draft night, and NHL Trade Rumors quoted the deal as "very close." Days later he played the Penguins in a 1-0 Dallas win. He is still in Dallas, and the Stars should be glad.

Robertson has 26 points in 23 games and 13 in his last ten, on 73 shots. His own shooting is normal, 13.7% against a league rate of 13.4%, so his 10 goals are honest. The flag is around him: Dallas has scored 8.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which pads the assist column. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 14th among forwards in value, with his team creating chances at a 98th percentile rate when he played, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his scoring chances from the slot in the 90th percentile. A shooter who scored 45 goals last season and keeps getting to the net is the kind of player you keep, not trade.
headline: The Robertson trade that nearly happened
